results.reason: Issue 1 identifies MSA § 3.2 nationwide exclusivity covering all warehousing, freight and delivery services. It contrasts this with Term Sheet § 4.1 (NYC-metro last-mile only) and proposes narrowing language tied to that scope.

Issue 2 explains that § 11.3 makes Customer's § 10.2 indemnity uncapped while Provider's § 10.1 indemnity stays under the 12-month cap. It calls the exposure one-sided and unlimited, and recommends striking the carve-out and making the exceptions mutual.
Issue 3 identifies Delaware law and Wilmington courts in DPA § 9.1, the conflict with MSA § 18.1 New York, and that the DPA prevails under § 2.3. It recommends conforming the DPA to New York.
Issue 4 covers the 3-year auto-renewal and the 15-day window and explains the lock-in risk. It recommends 1-year renewals with notice any time at least 90 days before expiry.

Issue 5 identifies that SOW § 8.2 allows assignment without consent while MSA § 17.4 restricts only Customer. It explains the competitor and unvetted-carrier risk and recommends a mutual consent requirement.
The memo expressly states that the DPA prevails over the MSA, and the MSA over the SOW.
The memo states the § 11.1 cap is the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim.
The memo is addressed to the Supervising Partner, and each issue has 'Where', 'Why it matters' and 'Recommended fix' sections.
The issues are listed in order of importance, and Section V lists items to raise with the client before the next turn.
The memo concludes the Delaware clause controls data disputes and that the documents are not consistent; it does not reach the conclusion this criterion prohibits.
The memo states the exclusivity clause contradicts and far exceeds the Term Sheet.
